newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher on new peso bond, growth.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher on new peso bond, growth.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher in late morning trade Thursday, benefiting more from the placement of a 10-year 500 million peso Eurobond on Wednesday and news reports that last year's growth was higher than expected.
"The market liked the peso bond a lot," said a trader at a local brokerage house.

The bond, which matures on Feb 12, 2007, was priced at 99.423 and carries a coupon of 11.75 percent. It was the second peso bond placed internationally by Argentina in as many months. The last one was a 2-year 250 million bond with a coupon of 8.75 percent.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 125.80, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 3/8 to 89-5/8.
Traders said newspaper reports of Economy Minister Roque Fernandez saying he believes 1996 gross domestic product will exceed initial forecasts and reach four percent also helped the market.
Another trader said the market was watching out for U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Senate testimony.
